Card Game

Seba

Seba is a card game of creatures from every culture's myths: dragons, kappa, firebirds, sea serpents and the gods of old pantheons. Open a free pack, peel five stickers and fill your bestiary. Nearly every card shows a public-domain artwork from Wikimedia Commons, The Met, the Cleveland Museum of Art or the Art Institute of Chicago, credited on the card with the creature's tradition and a short description. Rarity means something: legendary cards are the creatures the whole world knows, rare ones are told in only a few languages. Named after Albertus Seba, the 18th-century Amsterdam apothecary whose book of curiosities put real animals beside dragons and a seven-headed hydra.

Features

  • A free pack every hour, two kept in store, and a push when they are ready
  • Over 900 creatures and gods, from Greek and Norse myth to Japanese yōkai
  • Historic artworks from museum open-access collections, credited on every card
  • Twelve regions to complete, from the Celtic isles to the Americas
  • Friends by code, one-for-one trades and a friends leaderboard
  • The first player to find a card has their name on every copy
  • Guest play; packs are never sold
